dimension.category_description: How visible stages, dialogue states, histories, task decompositions, and session boundaries organize progress over time.
dimension.classification_boundary: The process structure must be exposed to users; hidden chains of model calls are excluded.

candidates.title: ChaCha: Leveraging Large Language Models to Prompt Children to Share Their Emotions about Personal Events
candidates.why: ChaCha provides the most complete runtime realization of the pattern: it maintains a current conversational phase, applies a phase-specific test to dialogue history after every message, and explicitly decides whether to remain or transition.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: Selected over Orchid-Creator because the evidence specifies persistent runtime state and per-turn transition computation, whereas Orchid-Creator’s excerpt primarily establishes the authoring representation.
candidates.pattern_summary: The sequence of conversational turns is governed by an authored control structure — a finite state machine, a protocol tree, a fixed phase sequence, a structured prompting scheme — rather than by the model's turn-by-turn discretion.
candidates.structural_signature: A graph or ordered stage list exists as an inspectable (often editable) object: nodes carry what the agent says or does, edges carry conditions evaluated on the interlocutor's response. The current node is persistent state, and a transition is computed at every turn, so the reachable next turns are a function of position in the structure.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: I reversed the top two consensus candidates because ChaCha’s excerpt demonstrates more of the full structural signature at runtime, including current-phase tests and a stay-or-advance decision on every turn. I also promoted rid 4906 over consensus-ranked rid 9621: TeamWise is a useful hybrid of authored sequence and generated utterances, but its evidence does not expose transition rules or persistent state. No score adjustment exceeds 0.3. All three selections rely on short excerpts rather than complete system descriptions, and none provides outcome evidence. In particular, Orchid-Creator’s excerpt does not confirm runtime state persistence, while rid 4906’s excerpt does not establish how visibly or directly end users can inspect or edit the four-state structure.

candidates.over_the_runner_up: Selected over the music-psychotherapy tool because its editable story graph and author-defined transitions more clearly establish that the control structure is inspectable and user-authored.

candidates.title: Criticmate: Stagewise Human-AI Co-Critique in Single-Screen UI Evaluation
candidates.why: Criticmate makes a fixed Perception–Comprehension–Projection sequence its central interaction structure, gives each stage a distinct epistemic role, and preserves editability without letting users author the sequence.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: It ranks above rid 4036 because its stages do more than organize task completion: they deliberately separate observation, interpretation, and action to prevent premature critique, making the pipeline more distinctive and conceptually transferable.
candidates.pattern_summary: Work advances through an ordered series of stages that is fixed by the designer before the user arrives.
candidates.structural_signature: A stage list S1…Sn exists in the system independent of any particular input, and each stage has its own module, section, or screen. The surface encodes the order (sections laid out in workflow order, a guided sequence of overlays, a chain of modules each consuming the previous one's output), and advancement is by completing or passing a stage rather than by free navigation. The number and identity of stages are constant across runs.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: The final selection follows the top three in the consensus order; no score was adjusted by more than 0.3. I slightly raised rid 4036 and rid 10222 because their evidence directly establishes visible phase structure or an ordered workflow panel. Readers should distrust any implied effectiveness claims: the supplied excerpts establish workflow design, not measured outcomes. Advancement enforcement is also not fully documented for any pick; Criticmate's evidence comes only from the abstract, rid 4036 from a figure caption, and CoAutoML's quote shows progress visibility but not explicit navigation constraints.

candidates.over_the_runner_up: It ranks above rid 10222 because the analysis–edit–review order has a stronger necessary dependency and closes a concrete safety loop, whereas CoAutoML's evidence chiefly establishes visible step-by-step progress.

candidates.title: From Visual to Multimodal Programming: Designing an Interface to Externalize Decomposition Thinking for Novice Learners
candidates.why: Spark turns a runtime, user-articulated goal into visible, structured steps and then enacts those steps through a robot, providing the clearest evidence of both input-specific decomposition and separate handling.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: Selected over ProDec because the evidence explicitly includes enactment of the generated steps, while ProDec’s excerpt establishes an editable dependency structure but not sequential execution.
candidates.pattern_summary: A goal supplied at runtime is broken into smaller sub-parts, and the parts are produced or handled serially rather than in one shot.
candidates.structural_signature: An input goal is transformed into an ordered list of sub-parts whose length and identity are computed per input (by the system, the user, or both). Each sub-part is executed or generated separately, in sequence, and appears as a discrete step in the interface; the final artifact is assembled from the parts. The sequence exists only for this goal — a different goal yields a different sequence.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: I retained the consensus top three but reordered the first two: Spark (rid 10246) is the strongest structural match because its evidence covers both visible decomposition and enactment, while ProDec’s evidence does not establish serial execution. No score adjustment exceeds 0.3. Readers should distrust any stronger claim that these excerpts fully demonstrate the structural signature: none explicitly confirms final-artifact assembly; ProDec does not explicitly show serial execution, Spark does not state that steps remain editable before advancement, and CoExplorer only implies that the proposed phases are subsequently handled in sequence.

candidates.title: ProDec: Automated Prompt Decomposition
candidates.why: ProDec converts each programming prompt into its own set of dependency-linked subtasks and exposes those reasoning steps for visual inspection and modification, closely matching the pattern’s variable decomposition and editability requirements.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: Selected over CoExplorer because ProDec exposes explicit subtasks and permits their modification, whereas CoExplorer shows collaboratively refined phases but leaves separate phase execution largely implicit.

candidates.title: Data Has Entered the Chat: How Data Workers Conduct Exploratory Visual Analytic Conversations with GenAI Agents
candidates.why: The Thread panel turns modifications into a navigable history whose prior entries can be reopened and refined, providing the clearest evidence of the pattern’s defining return-and-continue operation.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: It outranks Smartboard because the evidence explicitly supports continuing work from a historical record, whereas Smartboard demonstrates synchronized rollback but not subsequent refinement.
candidates.pattern_summary: Prior states and actions are retained as first-class records rather than discarded when superseded.
candidates.structural_signature: Every state change appends an addressable record (a version, a modification entry, an accept/reject/edit event, a timestamped frame). The interface renders the record set as a navigable structure — a list, a stream, a timeline — and supports two operations over it: returning to a past state and continuing from there, and traversing the sequence in temporal order. Records survive the session and the same view may serve live and retrospective inspection.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: I promoted rid 14005 over consensus-ranked rid 11931 to ensure the final set covers explicit chronological playback; the two higher selections already provide stronger evidence for restoration and, in rid 10412, continuation. No score was adjusted by more than 0.3. The set should not be read as proving every clause of the signature in every exemplar: rid 10412 does not explicitly establish playback or cross-session persistence; rid 14039 does not explicitly show playback or continued work after reversion; and rid 14005 is retrospective and does not support resuming or branching from a past state. Evidence for the first two also comes from figure text rather than a fuller interaction account.

candidates.title: Curompt: A Spatially Situated Interface for Generative AI in 3D Design Software
candidates.why: Per-object chat logs retain local change provenance while a global timeline makes every AI action revertible, combining addressable records with consequential workspace restoration.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: It outranks Smartboard because its complementary local and global histories expose both what changed and a workspace-wide rollback mechanism, making the design more transferable than a domain-specific tactic-state tree.

candidates.why: Its class-wide timeline supports inspection at any recorded point and variable-speed replay, offering the strongest direct realization of the pattern’s temporal-traversal operation.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: It displaces Smartboard because explicit variable-speed playback covers a required part of the structural signature that Smartboard’s selectable rollback tree does not demonstrate.
